regime: Energy-led stagflation-lite: Brent above $115, core inflation re-accelerating, hiring near zero and a Fed priced to hike again in December; long yields near 5% and stretched valuations
summary: The regime has hardened since Monday: Brent reached a six-month high of $116.72, WTI is up 77% over a year, UMich 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%, and futures still price a December hike at 78% (about 4.47% by mid-2027). Payrolls average +51k over 3 months while claims stay low, so the Fed can keep tightening without a labor crisis. Long-duration growth and AI-capex names remain the most fragile (SOXX -15.5% in a month), while energy, defense with record backlogs, quality health care and pricing-power defensives keep leading. The portfolio keeps its four holdings, raises stops on the winners, adds EOG as a pullback candidate and drops GE Vernova, whose setup broke.
drivers: Iran war and Hormuz risk: Brent $116.72, WTI $103.5, oil volatility 56 (87th percentile)
Fed funds futures: Dec 9 hike 78%, implied 4.47% by June 2027
10Y Treasury 4.99% and 10Y real yield about 2.8%, both near 10-year highs; equity risk premium negative
Core CPI 3-month annualized 3.4% and PPI 6.3% y/y: pipeline inflation still rising
AI capex doubts after Meta's capex hike; semis -11 pp vs SPY over 1 month
Energy +16 pp and health care +7 pp vs SPY over 3 months
risks: A durable Iran ceasefire drops oil below $85 and reverses energy leadership quickly
The Fed overtightens into a labor contraction (claims above 250k), hurting cyclicals and insurers
A broad AI-led de-rating with market cap/GDP at 258% drags defensives too
A sharp bond rally (10Y below 4.6%) would favour the growth names the portfolio underweights
